Plan: point-to-point measurements on the plots (issue #80)¶

Branch: 80-point-measurements, from main at 3779b49. Status: implemented (2026-10-22). Tested with a virtual X server (Xvfb) and synthetic input. The user tested it on XQuartz (2026-10-22).

1. Goal¶

Issue #80 asks for these items:

  1. Put a marker on a point of a plot (for example, the top of a pulse edge): the waterfall, or the AM, FM and PM plots.

  2. Put a second marker, and see the difference between the two points in the units of the axis, horizontally and vertically.

  3. Examples: the time between two pulse edges, the time between two pulses.

2. Starting point (main)¶

  • The time markers (T1, T2) and the frequency markers (F1, F2) are lines. The status bar shows dT, 1/dT and dF. They do not measure a value on the Y axis, and they cannot be put at a point of the signal with one action.

  • All time plots and the waterfall have one time axis, and the spectrum and the waterfall have one frequency axis (ImPlot axis links). So a time difference between two different plots is correct.

  • ImPlot 0.16 has DragPoint and Annotation. App::valueAt and App::wfValueAt read the plotted data.

3. Decisions¶

Question

Decision

Reason

A point on a time plot: free, or on the trace?

On the trace. Only the time is kept; the value is read from the plotted data at each frame

A free point measures the pointer, not the signal. When you zoom in, the demodulator calculates again at a finer resolution, and the marker stays on the trace

How to put a marker

M on the hovered plot, or Alt+click. Shift+M clears

Ctrl+click (tune), Shift+click (play) and right-click (menus, box zoom) are already used. M was free

Snap

When placed, the marker goes to the largest or the smallest value within ±8 px, if that value is at least 3 px nearer to the pointer than the sample under it

A click a little above a pulse goes to its top. A click on an edge stays on the edge. Noise on a flat top does not move the marker to the side

dT between two plots

Yes

The axes are shared, so it is correct, and the issue’s examples need it (a pulse in AM, a chirp in FM)

Value difference

Only on the same quantity: the same plot, or I with Q

Other pairs have different units

Signed differences

P2 minus P1

The sign tells the order. 1/dT uses the absolute value

A marker out of the view

The time plots keep the last value that was read with the same demodulator settings. The waterfall shows ?

The demodulator calculates only the view. To measure between two far-apart pulses, you zoom in on each one

Live mode

Not available

The data moves under the markers

4. Implementation¶

File

Change

src/dsp/measure.*

MeasPlot, PointMarker, the rules for which differences apply, nearestIndex, snapIndex. No ImGui, so measure_check tests it

src/app/app_measure.cpp

Placing, dragging and drawing the markers, the label at P2 and the status bar text

src/app/app.cpp

drawPoints and pointInput in the spectrum, the waterfall and endTimePlot. The status bar. Shift+M. A new file clears the markers. A new sample rate or center frequency moves them, as it moves the other markers

src/app/app_menu.cpp, app_export.cpp

View → Point markers, Clear point markers, the waterfall menu, the keyboard help

src/io/session.*, app_session.cpp

"points" in the session file. The version stays 1: an older session has no "points" and gets the defaults

src/app/platform_x11.cpp

macOS: when the Command key and Alt are on the same X modifier, the key that is down tells them apart (see below)

Alt and Command on one X modifier¶

On macOS, wvt reads the X modifier of the Meta and Super keys as Command, and sends it as Ctrl (issue #72). Xvfb puts Alt_L and Meta_L on the same key and modifier (Mod1), and XQuartz can do this with some key settings. Then Alt+click came to wvt as Ctrl+click and tuned the channel. Now, when a state has a modifier that holds both, wvt uses the Alt or Command key that is down (from the key events) to tell them apart. Linux builds do not change (cmdMask is 0).

5. Tests¶

  • measure_check: the nearest sample, the snap (a peak, a valley, an edge, a blanked sample, noise on a flat top), the difference rules, the plot names.

  • session_check: the points write and read back. A session without points, and a point on an unknown plot, read as “not set”.

  • On the screen (Xvfb, XTest input): M and Alt+click put P1 and P2 on the AM trace, dT and dAM in the status bar and the label; zoom in keeps the markers on the trace; a waterfall marker and an FM marker give dT only; a session with points opens and saves again.

6. Later¶

  • Snap to the 50 % point of an edge (rise and fall time measurements).

  • Markers in live mode, on a frozen view.
